# Reproduce AquaTrajectories v0.2.1

**Official immutable source release:** [AquaTrajectories v0.2.1](https://github.com/stefanosbalaskas/AquaTrajectories/releases/tag/v0.2.1), published **23 November 2026**. The released analytical core accepts externally supplied 2D/3D trajectories and does **not** require a video detector or identity tracker. The complete source archive and qualification evidence are attached to the release.

<div class="aqt-statusbar" role="group" aria-label="v0.2.1 release qualification">
<div><strong>Public R API</strong><span>188 documented exported R functions</span></div>
<div><strong>Measured coverage</strong><span>100.0000% instrumented R expressions · zero uncovered</span></div>
<div><strong>Cross-platform source gate</strong><span>Linux · Windows · macOS</span></div>
</div>

The exact v0.2.1 source archive passed strict `R CMD check` without errors, warnings or notes on all three operating systems. The measured `covr` report recorded **100.0000% R executed-expression coverage** and **zero uncovered expressions**; the release also qualified an independently reproduced synthetic trajectory-to-report example and **24 workloads per OS** covering 2D/3D analysis. These are software-execution tests, not fish-detection precision, biological identification or calibrated underwater XYZ error rates.

## Reproduce the locked synthetic 17 rows example

The redistributable source fixture contains 17 rows for three **invented** fish. It includes missing observations, a frame discontinuity and an excessive displacement. The known correct answer is **10 accepted adjacent movements totaling 10 cm**. Its unchanged input SHA-256 is:

`b940aedc80b9ca0a2355b5fcc1912cc233ecf6318044bed4d7449ca7ee0be2bc`

| Invented track | Original rows | Eligible adjacent steps | Accepted distance |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|
| 0001 | 5 | 3 | 3 cm |
| 0002 | 6 | 3 | 3 cm |
| 0003 | 6 | 4 | 4 cm |
| **Total** | **17** | **10** | **10 cm** |

From a checkout of the **exact v0.2.1 tag**, with R, Python 3 and the R package dependencies installed:

```sh
git clone --branch v0.2.1 --depth 1 https://github.com/stefanosbalaskas/AquaTrajectories.git
cd AquaTrajectories
R CMD INSTALL .
Rscript scripts/release05_example.R release05-example
python scripts/release05_verify.py --out release05-example
```

The R example writes an original-row QC ledger, publication graphics, SHA-256 inventory, explanatory report and source-to-figure links. The independent Python standard-library verifier re-derives the known movement and inspects exported evidence, without calling R. Use **new output directories** when rerunning. This is a synthetic software example; it does not validate real fish trajectories.

## M10: exact-v0.2.1 numerical replay on frozen real inputs

A separately conducted M10 audit installed the exact published v0.2.1 R archive in an isolated Windows R library and reran the **R analytical components** of historical M07–M08 using source-hash-verified frozen five-sequence BrackishMOT tables and the previously archived reference-matching ledger. It obtained **65/65 R–Python numerical comparisons**: 59 matching finite values and six mutually undefined values. This exact-version check supports **numerical reproducibility conditional on those frozen inputs**, not fresh inference from original footage.

The recorded analysis contains 6,621 publisher fish-reference observations and 2,830 external-model track rows. At the primary IoU 0.50 threshold, 374/6,621 published positions matched a track output and 265/6,498 original adjacent reference steps retained a matched continuous model ID. Conditional position and step errors among these matches cannot be generalized to unseen fish positions or interpreted as whole-school biological accuracy.

Read the [bounded M10 evidence summary](https://github.com/stefanosbalaskas/AquaTrajectories/blob/main/docs/M10_ANALYTICAL_V021_REPLAY_SUMMARY.md) and [M08 source-based protocol](https://github.com/stefanosbalaskas/AquaTrajectories/blob/v0.2.1/docs/BRACKISH_MEASUREMENT_VALIDATION_M08.md). The full original video, annotations and external detector weights are not redistributed with the site. An independent scientist must acquire the original data under the source's licence terms to reproduce the complete reference-conditional study.

## Performance evidence and limitations

The release ran **24 workloads per OS**, including 2D/3D trajectory path summaries, group geometry, source-row QC and publication figure specifications. Actual benchmark elapsed times and memory allocations depend on the runner environment. A historical v0.1.2 benchmark recorded, for example, 20,000-row 2D group geometry medians of 3.2856 seconds (Linux), 2.2616 seconds (Windows) and 2.0713 seconds (macOS); these are **not controlled platform comparisons** and are **not claimed as newly collected v0.2.1 run times**. Allocated R memory is not maximum process-resident memory.

For source-specific performance measurement, consult the [current v0.2.1 qualification evidence archive](https://github.com/stefanosbalaskas/AquaTrajectories/releases/tag/v0.2.1). For the earlier numerical source fixture and historical benchmark methodology, see the [v0.1.2 Release05 protocol](https://github.com/stefanosbalaskas/AquaTrajectories/blob/v0.1.2/docs/RELEASE05_REPRODUCIBLE_RESEARCH.md).
